input.rationale: Section 13.5 vests our own interface code and hosting Developments in Commerce One whenever Commerce One supports them on an ongoing basis — an assignment of Customer IP to the Vendor with no licence back, which is walk-away territory under this rule. Redline deletes the "unless supported" reversal so Developments created by us stay ours while Commerce One keeps its pre-existing materials and the Software itself (Section 2.8, which is acceptable). We also note that ownership of enhancements to the Software developed by us is left to future negotiation.

input.quote: Commerce One hereby grants to Corio a fee-bearing, perpetual and irrevocable, nonexclusive, nontransferable (except in accordance with Section 14.1 of this Agreement), right and license in the Territory
input.rationale: The hosting licence is perpetual and irrevocable, permits unlimited sublicensing to our Customers, survives termination (Section 11.3), is transferable to a successor via Section 14.1, and Section 14.8 confirms we may subcontract delivery of the Corio Services; the internal-use licence is perpetual and fully paid up. Affiliates are not expressly named and the Territory is limited to North America (with an expansion mechanism in Section 2.10) — noted, but the grant meets the fallback on its material terms.
